Messages.Author: Paul Hans Steiner
Messages.Body:
Because strikes are resolved individually can one damage prevention card
be used to prevent multiple damage points. I'm talking skin of rocks
not flesh of marbles which is pretty clear on this. Simple scenerio to
make my question clear.
Vamp A punches Vamp B who punches A back.
Vamp B plays skin of Rock at superior (prevent 2 damage)
Vamp A plays blur at minor for one additional strike which is a punch
for 1.
vamp B takes a point of damage or Prevents it with the unused skin of
rock.

Also just to confirm if Basilla is given sup Celerity she wouldn't get
to play additional strikes as the opposing vamp is torporized by the
first punch.(assuming nothing silly) I believe this comes straight from
the rulebook

Vamp B cannot prevent with the Skin Of Rock he played on the "prevention
step" of the previous strike resolution. He must use another card to prevent
the incoming damage.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Paul Hans Steiner wrote:
>
> Because strikes are resolved individually can one damage prevention card
> be used to prevent multiple damage points. I'm talking skin of rocks
> not flesh of marbles which is pretty clear on this. Simple scenerio to
> make my question clear.
> Vamp A punches Vamp B who punches A back.
> Vamp B plays skin of Rock at superior (prevent 2 damage)
> Vamp A plays blur at minor for one additional strike which is a punch
> for 1.
> vamp B takes a point of damage or Prevents it with the unused skin of
> rock.

Excess damage prevention cannot be saved for later use, nor can it be
retroactively used to prevent previously-applied damage.

A single damage prevention effect can be used to prevent damage done from
different sources, however, so long as all the damage being prevented is
inflicted at the same time (hand strike and Wolf Companion, e.g.)

> Also just to confirm if Basilla is given sup Celerity she wouldn't get
> to play additional strikes as the opposing vamp is torporized by the
> first punch.(assuming nothing silly) I believe this comes straight from
> the rulebook

Right (if "silly" includes damage prevention and dodge :-)
